content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early-to-mid forecast horizon (especially 1–10 days ahead), particularly after recent spikes.
- Overestimates prices after sharp upward moves (e.g., 70+ → 75+), often overshooting by 2–5% and failing to reflect mean reversion.
- Underestimates prices in late forecast horizon (15–30 days) when true values show upward drift or volatility.
- Shows persistent lag in capturing downward trends; delays reaction to price drops by 2–5 days.
- Tends to overfit recent high volatility periods, leading to overconfidence in short-term spikes.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model fails to adjust forecasts toward historical averages when prices deviate >3σ.
- Avoids “rebound” patterns after sharp declines — underpredicts recovery, especially in 10–20 day windows.
- Overly optimistic in low-volatility periods, failing to account for structural support or floor prices.
